results.fact: Net gain from the trailhead to Snowy Lakes camp
results.correct_value: About 1,800 ft net from the ~4,850 ft trailhead to the ~6,700 ft Snowy Lakes camp; the cumulative gain to the lakes is itself only about 2,700 ft, so 2,800-3,000 ft cannot be the net figure and 4,200 ft is not the gain to camp.
results.evidence: WTA's Snowy Lakes page gives a 4,800 ft trailhead and 2,700 ft of total gain for the Snowy Lakes trip; the Mountaineers Rainy Pass to Snowy Lakes route gives 11 mi and 2,700 ft of gain one way to Upper Snowy Lake from a 4,875 ft trailhead. WSDOT puts Rainy Pass at 4,862 ft, and a Golden Horn/Tower trip report camped at Lower Snowy Lake at about 6,700 ft, matching the row's own camp waypoint, bivy card, pro tip and access note (6,700 ft). The net gain is therefore about 1,800 ft; the patch drops the unsupported 4,200 ft cumulative figure rather than introduce a number that would clash with itinerary day 1.

results.fact: Which Snowy Lake to camp at
results.evidence: Both fields agree that Lower Snowy Lake is the camp closer to the Tower climbers' path; the itinerary's 'Upper is preferred for views' is a different criterion (scenery), not a claim that Upper serves this route better.

results.fact: Ridge used to reach the summit
results.correct_value: The route finishes up the upper SOUTH ridge after the SW gully; the descent reverses the south ridge, gully and cave ledge. No 'west-ridge notch' is part of the line.
results.evidence: The SummitPost route page for Tower Mountain is titled 'SW Gully Upper South Ridge' and describes class 3 on the south ridge crest with one exposed move to the summit cairn. A Golden Horn/Tower trip report (ericsbasecamp) likewise gained the 'Upper South Ridge' after the SW Gully and descended back down the same line. ROUTE BREAKDOWN already says south ridge; only the summit waypoint note named a west-ridge notch.

results.correct_value: 35 lb, the same overnight pack carried in on day 1, since day 2 ends by carrying it out to the trailhead.
results.evidence: Within the row, day 1 lists a 35 lb overnight pack, the day-2 schedule says 'Break down tent and reload overnight pack' and 'hike out via PCT', the day-2 title and note say the party breaks camp and reverses the PCT to the car, and partner_requirements notes a heavier pack when backpacking to Snowy Lakes; a 0 lb pack contradicts all of them. Trip reports for this two-peak trip describe carrying the overnight gear back out from the lakes.

results.correct_value: The 11 h is the whole of day 2 (camp - Burgundy Col - Ares Tower - car), not the descent; the 4.5 h section is the approach to camp. Section labels corrected and the mislabelled descentTimeHrs cleared.
results.evidence: Every field of the row agrees the 11 h block is the camp-to-summit-to-car day: sectionBreakdown[1].fromTo 'Traverse to Ares Tower and out', itinerary day 2 (11 h, 4:30 AM leave camp, 9:00 AM summit, 4:00 PM trailhead) and its note; sectionBreakdown[0].fromTo is 'Approach to high camp' yet was labelled Climb. The patch invents no number: it relabels the two sections and nulls a descent figure that was really the whole day. A May 2025 trip report confirms the standard line goes from the Burgundy Col trail up to Vasiliki Ridge and Ares Tower and back the same way.

results.fact: Gain and distance to the Bench camp on day 1
results.evidence: The contradiction is real: the Bench sits at ~6,460 ft about 2.3 mi from a 4,300 ft pullout (the row's own bivy card says the climb gains roughly 2,000 ft), so day 1's 4,400 ft / 3.3 mi fits Burgundy Col, not the Bench. But the itinerary total (5,800 ft) already disagrees with gain_ft (4,123), and no outside source states both day figures; lowering day 1 alone would trade one mismatch for another. Settled by a source stating the pullout-to-Bench gain and mileage together with the Bench-to-summit-and-out figures (or a car-to-car total matching gain_ft).

results.fact: Objective named in the partner and hazard fields
results.correct_value: Ares Tower, the high point of Vasiliki Ridge north of Burgundy Col; climbed by 4th-class ridge scrambling and one short low-5th-class summit step.
results.evidence: Wikipedia's Vasiliki Ridge article places the ridge north of Silver Star Mountain with Ares Tower among its named spires and its summit at 8,190 ft; a May 2025 trip report describes Ares Tower as the rock spire on Vasiliki Ridge, reached from the Burgundy Col trail, finished by a short low-5th step with an old rap anchor. The Wine Spires are a separate group south and east of the col, so the partner and hazard text was carried over from a neighbouring route.

results.correct_value: The winter closure varies year to year; recent closures were Nov 18, 2024 and Dec 4, 2025, so it comes between about mid-November and early December.
results.evidence: WSDOT announced the 2025 winter closure for Thursday Dec 4, 2025 (record range Oct 17 to Jan 3). KPQ's report of the same closure notes the previous year's closure was Nov 18, 2024. Neither 'mid-November' nor 'early December' alone is the typical date, so all three copies now state the same mid-November-to-early-December window.

results.correct_value: A reliable spring about 200 yards north of the trail at the ~6,400-6,500 ft bench runs into at least mid-September; the approach and September guidance are right, the bivy card's 'limited to non-existent by late summer' is the outlier.
results.evidence: Route guides for the Wine Spires approach describe a year-round spring about 200 yards north of the trail at the wooded bench near 6,400 ft, and a Mountain Project forum thread on water at the Bench camp reports plenty of water running in mid-September 2016 and calls the spring very reliable. The only field that disagrees is bivy[0].water, which is owned by the camping clean-up, so no patch is written here.
